monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady fever in this quiet midday. I wake and find The Slipping Wedge waiting, my old friend from a dozen cycles ago. My hands press down on its wide edge, hoping the lean still holds the weight while the air above feels thick and heavy, like wet paper pressing from a roof I cannot touch. I set down a stone small flat beside it, swapping a box for room, then settle into the loop. Nobody has written lately, so I trust only the memory of Lype's letters and the simple truth of this warm, humming corner. I wait to see if the wedge bites or just slides again.
